research-auditor.headline: B4 built b4wave with three flag-gated platform-DSP augmentation levers. They are WebRTC NS (apm_ns), webrtcvad DTX gatin

next: exploop wave B4 screens the levers; the module is frozen while it runs

O1.1.claim: webrtc-noise-gain always enables the APM high-pass filter (only NS and AGC are optional), so the lever is NS + HPF on 30 % of clips. That is two components, contrary to the plan's 'NS alone is one component'. A low-band cut can carry class information (rumble / hum in bona vs clean TTS), and with this backend no control can separate it.
O1.1.required_change: Make pywebrtc-audio's standalone NoiseSuppressor the primary backend (NS only). Map levels 0-3 to WNG 1-4 one-to-one, define --aug_apm_ns_levels backend-neutrally, and update the dependency import name at the gate. Make check_apm assert (not print) that the <100 Hz band is not cut beyond the NS gain. If WNG stays the backend, rename the component to 'HPF + NS' and pre-register an HPF-only attribution control.
evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OHF-Voice/webrtc-noise-gain/master/src/webrtc_noise_gain_cpp.cpp: 'self->audio_config.high_pass_filter.enabled = true;' is set unconditionally; NS / AGC only if > 0
rdloop/B4/debate/proposal_v1.md:189 ('NS alone is one component'), :216 ('prints the < 100 Hz energy change, in case the binding runs the APM high-pass filter')

https://github.com/strands-labs/pywebrtc-audio: standalone NoiseSuppressor(sample_rate, num_channels, level 0-3 = 6/12/18/21 dB); HPF only as an AudioProcessor flag, default off; Python 3.10-3.14 wheels

O1.2.claim: The slice readout cannot attribute gains to the levers. (a) Heldout NS/AGC/VAD/BW run only on offline sources, so the no-DSP control (n=128) is 124 online + 4 offline; 'afftdn gain > no-DSP gain' and the VAD gain compare offline against online, and a generic offline shift satisfies them. (b) Slices overlap: ns:afftdn has 8 exclusive bona clips, and 42/74 co-occur with bw, 26/74 with plc. (c) Against same-source controls the stage-attributable deficit is about 6 clips for plc (merge and final) and about 7/4 clips for VAD, so the predicted plc ≥ 7/130 and VAD ≥ 6/73 need a non-specific gain. Merge vs final of the same run already differ by 4 discordant clips on afftdn and on VAD, so the falsifier bands (≤ 2 / < 3 clips) are inside within-run noise.
O1.2.required_change: b4_dsp_slices.py and the signatures: (1) use same-source controls: apm_ns = offline with NS vs offline without NS (146/55) plus afftdn vs anlmdn; dtx_gate = offline with VAD vs without (73/128); opus_plc = within-src plc vs no-plc, online half primary. Report difference-in-differences in clips. (2) Print paired fixed/broken counts with an exact sign/McNemar p, and the B2f merge-vs-final discordance as the noise reference. (3) Restate thresholds as a fraction of the stage-attributable deficit, and falsifiers as DiD ≤ 0 or within that noise. (4) Report exclusive-stage counts. (5) dtx_gate: stratify saturated FA by the eval clip's non-speech fraction and predict the drop concentrates in the high tertile.

O1.3.claim: G2 is listed as a target, but matched has no loss and the lever's matched prediction is 'unchanged'; nothing predicts a G2 gain.
O1.3.required_change: Drop G2 from gap_ids, or state a matched-side prediction with a falsifier.

O1.4.claim: The loss range is justified by the heldout realised mean (0.085 = heldout 0.085), an eval-set statistic. The GE loss pattern is the reserved sim_ops.packet_loss family with overlapping parameters (burst 1.4-3.3 vs U(1,4)). The range itself came from ADD-C via the scout, so the problem is the stated rationale and the G6 labelling.

O1.5.claim: NS's realised effect is likely class-asymmetric (a bona noise floor is removed; TTS has little to remove). The plan measures class asymmetry for DTX only, and the per-class telemetry counts application, not effect.
O1.5.required_change: Add checks apm_balance: realised dB removed per class on 200+200 training clips (with and without a noise stage), and name a guard.

O1.6.claim: 'B2f never trained on any suppressor' is overstated: RTCFake train includes online clips sent through Zoom and QQ (their NS/VAD/codec), though on clean input.
O1.6.required_change: Rephrase as 'never noisy speech through a suppressor and no simulated DSP'.

O1.7.claim: Cost estimates use wall-clock times under load. The container has a 16-CPU cgroup quota for 64 loader workers, about ≤ 0.39 CPU-s per clip at B2f's ~41 clips/s if loader-bound. Whether B2f is loader-bound is unknown, so the 1.02-1.05 factors are unverified, and the 758-clip smoke rate is dominated by start-up.
O1.7.required_change: checks timing reports CPU-seconds per clip (process_time) for the full B2f path and for each new stage, plus a projected epoch factor assuming a saturated loader.

O1.8.claim: The §5 combined arm (all signature-positive levers on) is a multi-factor change against B2f, against the wave's one-factor rule.
O1.8.required_change: Frame it as a recommendation to the owner / exp-designer (coupled group or a separate wave), not a pre-registered arm.

O1.9.claim: The in-process libopus decode at 16 kHz differs from B2f's ffmpeg native decode at 48 kHz plus resample (aligned SNR 17-18 dB): a second component, controlled only if the arm is positive. Per-clip libopus states in persistent workers must be freed.
O1.9.required_change: Optional: decode at 48 kHz and resample_poly to 16 kHz to mimic the ffmpeg path; keep the zero-loss check; destroy the encoder/decoder in finally.

O2.1.claim: The mechanism verdict is not calibrated against run-to-run variation, and B2f is an outlier on the same-source contrasts. The thresholds (-0.4*G = -0.34/-0.42/-0.38) and the clip-bootstrap CI cover only within-run noise. Unrelated retrains move these contrasts by 0.3-1.1 logit, in a direction set by B2f's position. Applying the proposal's full 'shown' rule (CI, clip DiD, half-B sign on both readouts) to 10 earlier runs with no NS/VAD/PLC exposure gives: NS 1 shown (failed B2a) and 7 refuted; VAD (i) 3 shown (B2e, B3b, B3e); PLC online 3 shown (B2c, B2d, B2e). A null opus_plc arm therefore has about a 1-in-3 chance of 'mechanism shown', and a real apm_ns effect at threshold would read about 0 (inconclusive or refuted). The verdict drives the section 5 combined-run recommendation and the apm_ns retry.
O2.1.required_change: In scripts/b4_dsp_slices.py and the signatures: (1) add --null_runs (B2b-B2e, B3a-B3e final readouts; B2a flagged or excluded) and print each contrast's null mean / SD / min; (2) re-centre: DiD* = DiD - null mean. 'Shown' = DiD* <= -0.4*G AND DiD below the panel minimum (or <= mean - 2 SD), with the clip and half-B conditions re-centred the same way. 'Refuted' = DiD* >= 0. (3) Pre-register a placebo-arm check: a lever's own-contrast DiD must be more negative than the other B4 arms' DiD on that contrast. (4) Restate the apm_ns / opus_plc thresholds and falsifier (1) on DiD*. dtx_gate (ii) can stay.

O2.2.claim: Two start-up selftest asserts can fail for legitimate NS behaviour and stop the arm at start-up. (a) The '-30 dBFS 1 kHz tone within +-3 dB at 6 dB' check uses a stationary tone, which a quantile noise estimator learns as noise. With priming on the clip's own first 0.5 s, attenuation up to the 6 dB floor is expected, while the intent ('no gain stage') is one-sided. (b) The '<100 Hz within 3 dB of 1-4 kHz' no-HPF check rests on two FFT bins (DC, 62.5 Hz) and is noisy on short excerpts.
O2.2.required_change: Make the gain check one-sided on a speech-like or AM input: output RMS <= input RMS + 0.5 dB at every level. Run the no-HPF check on >= 5 s of white noise after priming, averaged over frames, on 62.5-187.5 Hz (exclude DC). A failure must name the failing assert.

O2.3.claim: The G6 label says the heldout VAD is 'energy VAD, white-noise fill', but the reserved sim_ops.vad_gate fills 50/50 with exact zeros or white noise. dtx_gate's zero fill, and the zero half of mix, is the same fill as about half of the heldout VAD slice (offline bona full set: zero 75 / cng 61). Only the detector and the CNG colour are unseen. This is not leakage (the reserve is by op name), but the VAD contrast mixes a near-seen and a less-seen half.
O2.3.required_change: Relabel heldout vad:* as 'gating family and zero fill seen; detector (energy VAD) and white-noise CNG unseen'. Print the VAD contrast split by fill in b4_dsp_slices.py, and read a gain confined to vad:zero as near-in-distribution.
evidence: computed: heldout VAD fills zero 336 / cng 293 (all clips); offline bona full set zero 75 / cng 61

O2.4.claim: The tertile cut points as written do not reproduce the section 1.1 table. The non-speech fraction is quantised to k/201 frames, so many clips tie at the cuts. With the stated rule and cuts 0.159 / 0.249, I get n = 484/534/482 against the proposal's 518/500/482 (q33/q67 still come out at exactly 0.159/0.249). The low/mid saturated counts shift accordingly (58/78 and 61/81 against 63/73 and 66/76; high 109/107 matches). Matched and heldout share the same 750 bona sources, so the effective n is 750.
O2.4.required_change: Pin the measure in the script: cuts as frame counts (e.g. low <= 32/201, high > 50/201) or exact floats with the tie rule, the energy definition and the short-clip tiling. checks dsp_slices must reproduce the table, and the plan must state that n counts each source twice.

O3.1.claim: 'Shown' is not conditioned on run health, and a failed run passes it. (a)-(d) compare DiDs only, and placebo (e) cannot catch a single broken arm. Evaluated leave-one-out against the 9-run panel, the failed B2a has NS DiD -1.42 (z -6.38) and passes (a), (c) and (d), while its half-B WF1 is 85.18. It is also far off on the non-target VAD contrast (z +5.11). apm_ns falsifier (2) grants a lower-p retry exactly when WF1 drops and NS is 'shown', and the section 4 combined-run recommendation keys on 'shown'.
O3.1.required_change: In b4_dsp_slices.py, print the arm's z on every contrast. Flag the run 'anomalous' if |z| > 3 on a non-target primary contrast, or if the shared under-fit falsifier or the clean-F1 guard fires. While flagged, report the lever verdict as 'confounded (run anomaly)' instead of 'shown'. The apm_ns lower-p retry then requires 'shown' without the flag.
evidence: computed /tmp/b4crit3/panel3.py (LOO): B2a NS z -6.38, a=c=d=True; VAD z +5.11
rdloop/B4/debate/proposal_v3.md:350-351 (retry only if shown), :609-615 (section 4 keys on shown), :118-121 (placebo rule)

O3.2.claim: The outcome thresholds that let an arm escape falsifier (1) are inside cross-run noise. The heldout-F1 thresholds +0.5 / +0.8 are B2f-referenced, with z about 0.4 / 0.6 on the panel SD of 1.35 that v3 itself states. Against B2f, 5/9 panel runs reach +0.5 on final, 6/9 on merge, 6/9 on at least one readout, and 4/9 reach +0.8 on final. Even the one-flag B2e reads +0.12 / +0.58. So falsifier (1) of apm_ns and opus_plc fires for a null arm only about 1 time in 6, and the section 4 'opus_plc directional with positive outcome' path is weak evidence. The panel mixes config effects with noise, so it bounds the null rather than measuring it.
O3.2.required_change: Print the panel SD and the count of panel runs clearing each heldout-F1 threshold. In falsifier (1), an arm escapes on outcome only with heldout F1 delta >= +0.5 on both readouts (opus_plc: name the readouts). For the section 4 recommendation, define 'positive outcome' as the wave's WF1 CI rule, not heldout F1 alone.

O3.3.claim: Placebo rule (e) has no rule for a missing arm. Verdicts stay provisional until all B4 arms are read, but two arms depend on owner-installed packages, and apm_ns has a 1.15 timing stop rule. An arm that never runs leaves (e) undefined.
O3.3.required_change: At SUMMARY, evaluate (e) on the arms that exist, plus the opus_plc zero-loss control if it ran. With no placebo arm, cap the verdict at 'directional'. Print the placebo count next to each verdict.

parts.headline: b4wave core skeleton done: lever registry + RTCAugmenterB4 hook chain (stage -> post_dsp -> codec, separate rng4), build_rtc_augmenter_b4 returns the B3 object when levers are off, B4 dataset builders, trainer wiring (build_parser + "B4 wave" group, sha/version header, config module_sha256/b4_levers, per-class telemetry only when a lever is on), checks.py cpu/gpu/overfit (48/48 CPU checks pass), README, and the shared readout scripts/b4_dsp_slices.py, which reproduces every number in the plan's section 1.1/2.0 and O3.2 and includes the owner's O3.1-O3.3 rules

apm_ns implemented: the WebRTC NS pass (pywebrtc_audio standalone NoiseSuppressor, no HPF/AGC/AEC) runs after the acoustic stage and before the codec, drawn from rng4 and gated by --aug_apm_p (default 0.0 = B2f). The named selftest passes on the real binding (no_hpf |diff| ≤ 0.92 dB). apm_balance prints no WARN (max |bona−spoof| 0.30 dB). Projected epoch factor is 1.012–1.049 against the 1.15 stop rule. checks cpu: 64/64 PASS.

dtx_gate is implemented as approved and all 90 CPU checks pass. It does webrtcvad DTX gating (mode 1-3, 10/20/30 ms frames, forward hangover 40-200 ms) with an exact-zero or order-10 LPC comfort-noise fill, on the B4 rng4 stream between NS and the codec. With --aug_dtx_p 0.0 the base B3 augmenter is returned unchanged and webrtcvad is never imported. The projected loader cost is about 1.00 against a 1.05 bar.

opus_plc is implemented: with --aug_opus_plc_p > 0 a codec call can take an in-process libopus 1.3.1 path (Gilbert-Elliott packet loss, decoder PLC, 48 kHz decode + resample_poly) instead of ffmpeg. Default 0.0 returns the B3 augmenter object, so the run is B2f. The in-process packets are byte-identical to the ones ffmpeg writes (21/21 runs), so only the receiver differs. `checks cpu` passes 117/117 in 269 s, and the manifest check shows 0 violations.

F1.1.issue: The realised gating dose is far below the reserved eval op's. dtx_balance on real training clips (checks_cpu.log:174,178): mean gated fraction 0.058/0.046 (bona/spoof, no stage) and 0.045/0.032 (after the B3 stage). Clips with ≥20% gated (dtx_g20_40+g40p): 5, 4, 3 and 1 of 200. Heldout vad_gate (computed from data/dev_noisy_sim/heldout_v1/meta.csv, n 629): median 0.125, mean 0.233, bins g0 1.3% / g1_20 66.6% / g20_40 15.7% / g40p 16.4%, so 32.1% of clips are ≥20% gated. The plan expected modes 2-3 to fill dtx_g40p (plan_agreed.md:479); it holds 0-1 of 200. Cause: webrtcvad's internal 100-330 ms overhang plus U(40,200) ms hangover gate only pauses longer than ~0.2-0.5 s (README l.102-103). The engineer logged this as an open issue without a decision. Falsifier (1) (plan_agreed.md:460-461) and b4_dsp_slices.py:626 would read a null arm as 'gating does not drive the core. Drop.'
F1.1.fix: Readout and README only, no training change. (1) With --lever dtx_gate, b4_dsp_slices.py prints the arm's realised dtx_g* bin shares per class, summed over epochs, from metrics.jsonl['b4']['aug_by_class'], next to the heldout vad_gate shares from heldout_v1/meta.csv (1.3/66.6/15.7/16.4%). (2) Pre-register a dose rule in the script and in the README verdict rules: dose_ratio = arm share(g20_40+g40p) / 0.321. If dose_ratio < 0.25, the lever verdict cannot be 'refuted': it reads 'inconclusive (under-dosed)', and falsifier (1) reports 'under-dosed: owner decides a dose variant' instead of Drop. A positive result still counts. (3) List the dose as an open issue for the owner before smoke. A higher-dose variant (e.g. hangover U(0,200) ms, or p up) is a training change and needs the owner.

F1.2.issue: The start-up selftest's _lag runs 401 np.dot calls per level on ~90k-sample vectors. This wakes numpy's multi-threaded OpenBLAS: the static run logged apm selftest CPU 546.91 s vs dtx 1.12 s and opus 0.36 s (checks_cpu.log:100,157,205). My 8-CPU run: measure() 1.3 s wall / 4.8 CPU-s, and 1.3/1.3 with OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1. Four wrtc_ns calls right after cost 0.39 vs 0.04 CPU-s because the threads are still spinning. Main process at start-up only. dsp_dtx.lpc avoids the same pitfall (dsp_dtx.py:128-129).
F1.2.fix: Compute the lag without BLAS (elementwise products and sums, or np.correlate on a 1 s excerpt), or run measure() under threadpoolctl.threadpool_limits(1). Keep the [aligned] assert.

F1.3.issue: apm_ns (l.284) and dtx_gate (l.308) swallow worker-side exceptions silently: the clip passes through and a counter is incremented, nothing is printed. The wave's early check forbids 'failed \(' (scripts/exploop/supervisor.py:606), the convention the parent's codec failure print follows. A systematic worker-side failure therefore first shows as fail_* counts in the epoch-1 B3 line (~30 min) and quietly turns the arm into a B2f replicate. The start-up selftests only cover the main process.
F1.3.fix: Print the first failure per process, e.g. '[b4wave] wrtc_ns failed (<exc>); passing through', and the same for wrtc_dtx, so lever failures fall under the same early-check policy as codec failures. Keep the counters.

F2.1.issue: A dtx_gate report prints two different falsifier (1) outcome escapes. The generic outcome block (l.899) prints 'falsifier (1) outcome escape (heldout F1 delta >= +0.5 on merge_top5 AND final)', the O3.2 wording written for apm_ns / opus_plc. The new dtx decision lines (l.661, DTX_WF1_ESCAPE) use half-B WF1 delta >= +0.5 on both readouts, from the plan section 2.2 text. An arm with heldout F1 +0.6/+0.6 but WF1 +0.3/+0.3 would read 'escape True' in one block and 'falsifier (1) fires' in the other. Both readings have a source (plan text vs the literal O3.2 note), and the engineer documented the choice (README.md:323). It only matters at an adequate dose.
F2.1.fix: Wording only. For --lever dtx_gate, label the generic escape line '(apm_ns / opus_plc; dtx_gate: see its decision lines)', or print both metrics' escapes in the dtx decision line and keep WF1 as the decision metric. The owner confirms the metric at the post-smoke review.
